subject.title: fix(ollama): stop oversized stream records from growing memory

question: Is 16 MiB an acceptable fixed maximum for one native Ollama NDJSON record when upstream defines the framing format but no record-size ceiling?
rationale: The implementation is technically sound, but selecting an undocumented fail-closed record-size boundary is a compatibility choice that should be explicitly owned by the Ollama runtime reviewers.

options.title: Keep the 16 MiB cap
options.body: Accept the generous fixed boundary, rebase the branch, and merge once focused tests and required checks are green.

options.title: Revise the record policy
options.body: Require a different fixed threshold or another bounded policy before merge, with equivalent overflow and newline-reset proof.

recommendation.title: Keep the 16 MiB cap
recommendation.body: Accept the generous fixed boundary, rebase the branch, and merge once focused tests and required checks are green.

likelyOwner.reason: They reviewed and merged the original native Ollama streaming implementation and are the strongest available owner for its compatibility boundary.
